title: The swim score difference stayed positive with any 26 added input labels in one fixed leech cell group
abstract: We tested how unrecorded chemical inputs can change a reported activity difference in one leech ganglion. The main cell group had 40 recorded inputs to motor neuron DE-3R and 99 comparison cells. We kept all recorded input labels and measured repeated coherence scores fixed. Sorted score sums gave the smallest and largest possible mean difference for each number of added input labels. The swim difference of 0.219581 stayed positive for every choice of up to 26 added labels. A choice of 27 made it nonpositive. One shared 27-cell choice also made the left-bend difference nonpositive. The group of all mapped cells needed 33 added labels for swim and for both behaviors. Uniform selection of added labels kept the expected difference positive at every allowed count. Thus that reference does not cover omissions that depend on activity. These bounds apply only to the fixed cells and scores. They do not estimate missing inputs, sampling uncertainty or causal effects. False recorded labels, score errors, cells outside the group, one animal and few trials limit the result. The package has original code, aggregate results, source hashes, external retrieval steps and independent checks. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Smallest and largest possible swim score differences at selected counts of added input labels. Lines between points are guides. Dotted lines mark the first counts that can make the difference nonpositive. Dashed lines show means for uniform selection of added labels. Scores and recorded labels are fixed. The ranges are not confidence intervals.
